title: What the programme validator catches, and the one thing it cannot
purpose: A validator that reports PASS proves only that the checks it implements agree with each other. This record states which deliberate defects those checks actually caught in this package, and records a defect class they cannot catch, so a pass is not read as more than it is.
method: Copy the finished package to a scratch directory. Introduce one defect at a time. Run validate_programme.py against the copy. Restore the copy and confirm it passes again before the next defect. Each defect below was applied to a copy; this package was never modified for the test.

defects_caught.defect: A research record relinked to a different simulation case, breaking the one-to-one chain.
The status file inflated simulation_results from 5 to 6.
A research record marked AWARDED programme credit that no owner granted.
A recorded result value overwritten in results/SIM-002.json, manifest left untouched.
defects_caught.note: Caught for the right reason: the file no longer hashes to its locked value.

defect_not_caught.defect: A recorded result value overwritten in results/SIM-002.json, and the manifest then re-locked over the edit so every hash agrees again.
defect_not_caught.why: No check recomputes a simulation. The validator compares records to each other and to the locked hashes; it does not re-derive what the run should have produced. Once the hash is re-locked, a falsified number is internally consistent with everything the validator examines.
defect_not_caught.what_would_catch_it: Re-running the simulation from the recorded case configuration and code hash, by a party that did not write the model. That is independent reproduction, and it is a different activity from validation. It has not been performed for this package.

scope_evidence: The validator states this limit itself in its own scope field: it does not re-execute simulations and does not award programme credit. This record confirms that statement empirically rather than taking it on trust.
residual_risk_statement: A PASS from this validator means the evidence package is internally consistent and honestly labelled. It does not mean the numbers are true. Treating a PASS as scientific validation, or as authorization to release, would be a misuse of the tool.
